## Audit note (epic 3405-c0b7) — refined-bar guidance may resolve this deferred design decision

Re-triaging under the sharpened standard: an error code need not be narrow; prefer an **existing broad-but-accurate** code over new vocabulary, and reserve escalation for when NO existing code fits.

Applying that here: `ExpressionError` (execute-time input/step-output/loop-var/secret/env resolution failures) is not a provider-availability condition, so `llm_unavailable` MIS-fits it. The honest existing-vocab fit is **`command_failed`** ("an unclassified rebar command failure") — which accurately describes an execute-time wiring/resolution failure without asserting an outage.

This also dissolves the dbca-AC3 tension you flagged ("keep execute-time on llm_unavailable to protect genuine outages"): the correct discriminator is the exception TYPE, not the phase. Narrow `error_code_for` branch 6 to fire `llm_unavailable` only for `LLMUnavailableError` — then a genuine execute-time provider outage (raised as `LLMUnavailableError`) STILL maps to `llm_unavailable`, while `ExpressionError` (a `WorkflowError`, not an availability fault) falls to `command_failed`. No new vocabulary, no phase special-casing.

Suggest this may be **downgradable from an escalate/design-decision to ready-to-fix** (target code `command_failed`), unless an operator wants a finer `workflow_invalid`/`expression_unresolved` code — which the refined bar says to add only on demonstrated observable need. Not transitioning this ticket myself (read-only audit); flagging for the owner. See the observable sibling 7d47 (render_workflow, load-time) and the unifying recommendation on 5f96.

comments.author: Rebar Bot
comments.body:
## Decision (operator, 2026-08-30): Option B approved — add a dedicated `expression_unresolved` code

`ExpressionError` (execute-time workflow expression-resolution failure: unset input, missing
step output, loop var out of scope, unresolvable `${{ }}`, missing secret/env) will map to a
new **`expression_unresolved`** code, NOT `llm_unavailable` (misleading — asserts an outage)
and NOT `command_failed` (accurate but too vague to guide an agent's retry-vs-fix decision on
the `run_workflow` surface).

**Rationale / precedent.** gRPC canonical status codes reserve `UNAVAILABLE` for transient
outages and give caller/state faults specific codes, explicitly warning against dumping a
classifiable fault into the generic `UNKNOWN`/`INTERNAL` bucket (= our `command_failed`).
HTTP's 4xx-vs-5xx split says the same. `invalid_input` was rejected: `ExpressionError` also
fires for environment faults (missing secret, empty upstream output), so "invalid input" would
be a *different* misleading code.

**Implementation shape (low blast radius):**
- Set `error_code = "expression_unresolved"` as an attribute on `ExpressionError` (or
  `WorkflowError` if the whole family fits) so `error_code_for` branch 5 (explicit
  `error_code`) fires BEFORE branch 6 (`LLMError → llm_unavailable`). Only `ExpressionError`
  changes; other `LLMError`s untouched.
- Add `expression_unresolved` to `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES` (`src/rebar/_errors.py`) + the guardrail
  contract test `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_error_code_taxonomy_contract.py`.
- Tests through the REAL `run_workflow`/execute surface (per AC): a genuine execute-time LLM
  outage still returns `llm_unavailable`; an `ExpressionError` returns `expression_unresolved`.

**Separate follow-up (not this ticket):** narrow `error_code_for` branch 6 to fire
`llm_unavailable` only for `LLMUnavailableError` (reserve it for true outages) — a broader
cleanup with its own blast radius (sweep all `LLMError` subclasses). File discovered_from this
ticket when implemented.

Origin unchanged: 8a31 (blanket LLMError→llm_unavailable). Ready to move from
escalate/design-decision to ready-to-fix.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## DECISION NEEDED — what code should an execute-time `ExpressionError` map to? (currently `llm_unavailable`)

**The fault.** `ExpressionError` (`executor.py:251`) fires at EXECUTE time for wiring/state faults: an input not set, no such step output, a loop/map var out of scope, a missing secret/env, an unresolvable `${{ }}`. `error_code_for` already distinguishes families (`src/rebar/_errors.py`): branch 6 remaps workflow parse/lint/unknown-step faults to `invalid_input` (bug dbca), and the bare `WorkflowError` base is *deliberately* kept on `llm_unavailable` so a real LLM outage inside an execute step still reads as an outage (dbca AC3). `ExpressionError` is a `WorkflowError` subclass that falls through to that base — so it inherits `llm_unavailable` even though it is a caller/state wiring bug, not an outage.

**Prior art.** Bug `35ab` already moved the executor's unknown-step (a plan-authoring fault) to `invalid_input`; this is the sibling case one phase later.

**OSS grounding.** gRPC and HTTP deliberately separate "you sent something wrong / precondition unmet" (`INVALID_ARGUMENT`/`FAILED_PRECONDITION`, HTTP 4xx — do NOT retry) from "service is down" (`UNAVAILABLE`, HTTP 503 — retry later). Mapping a wiring bug to "unavailable" tells callers/alerting to retry a fault that will never self-heal and pollutes outage signals.

**Recommendation:** Reclassify `ExpressionError` → `invalid_input` (caller-input class), matching `35ab`, by giving it an explicit `error_code='invalid_input'` so it is honest regardless of branch order. This is coupled with **ce6b** (which narrows the `llm_unavailable` branch generally) — approve the two together so they don't collide.

compiled_state.description:
Discovered during the Step 7 sibling sweep of 35ab-f0e0-3e4a-4b72 (fightable-nirvanic-kitten).

## Site
`ExpressionError(WorkflowError)` is defined at `src/rebar/llm/workflow/executor.py:251` and raised from workflow execute-time expression resolution (`interpreter.py` and `executor.py`) for wiring/state faults: input not set, no such step output, loop/map var out of scope, missing secret/env, or unresolvable `${{ }}` expression.

## Symptom
`error_code_for(ExpressionError(...))` currently reaches the broad `LLMError`/`WorkflowError` branch and returns `llm_unavailable`. That asserts a provider outage for a caller/state wiring fault and encourages retries that will not self-heal.

## Operator decision
Latest DECISION NEEDED comment (operator-approved 2026-09-01) supersedes the earlier `expression_unresolved` option for this ticket: reclassify `ExpressionError -> invalid_input`, matching prior bug 35ab (executor unknown-step -> invalid_input) and dbca (parse/lint -> invalid_input). Give `ExpressionError` an explicit `error_code = "invalid_input"` so the mapping is honest regardless of branch order. Preserve dbca AC3 by ensuring genuine execute-time LLM outages still map to `llm_unavailable` through the true outage type/wrapper path. Implement this with ce6b's umbrella narrowing as one coherent change.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `ExpressionError` has an explicit `error_code = "invalid_input"` and `error_code_for(ExpressionError(...))` returns `invalid_input`, verified by a focused unit/contract test.
- [x] A real workflow execute-surface expression-resolution failure returns `invalid_input`, not `llm_unavailable`, verified through the real workflow execution surface or the smallest existing production error conversion seam that exercises the same exception.
- [x] A genuine LLM outage inside an execute step still returns `llm_unavailable`, verified by a focused test covering the preserved dbca AC3 path.
- [x] The implementation lands in the same Gerrit change as ce6b and references both tickets.

## Testing
Run the focused workflow/error taxonomy tests added or updated for this ticket with `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest -q`, then run `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint` and `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck`. After commit, run `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" rebar verify-commit-ticket HEAD` to verify ticket trailers.

File-impact update after implementation: this ticket is closed by the combined Gerrit #2482 commit with ce6b, so its recorded impact includes the shared taxonomy files and held-out compatibility tests touched by that single coherent change, not only `ExpressionError` itself.
